description: Explicit pinned SHAs for the cross-repository integrity workflow (.github/workflows/cross-repo-integrity.yml). Update deliberately, in the same PR as the change that requires a new pin, never silently.

data-connect.note: Merge commit of data-connect#116 into PDP-Connect/data-connect main (merged 2026-09-14T14:49:13Z), captured from main's head and confirmed an ancestor of main via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — never a PR head, for the reason the superseded-pin history below records. Moved from e5916d3a6 (data-connect#94's merge) because four further changes landed on data-connect main, each moving a different set of guarded bytes. (1) #106 `a707c4650` rewrote collector-runtime's durable outbox to carry artifact bytes through to upload, adding collector-runner/local-device-blob-capture/local-device-blob-spool to the packed dist/ and changing local-device-outbox. That retires the previous note's claim that collector-runtime is deliberately NOT re-vendored and that a fresh repack reproduces e274fb459 exactly: both were true at e5916d3a6 and are false here. (2) #112 `d425a7f38` vendors the claude_code connector sources (index.ts, schemas.ts, and the new artifact-capture.ts) into data-connect, which is what drift job (b) connector-sources compares. Those bytes are data-connectors#100's head 89ceb611a, verified byte-for-byte, so job (b) reconciles on #100 and NOT on main, which still predates those files — this repin lands first and #100 turns green on it, the ordering FIX106's plan describes. (3) #96 `4ade3ca01` moved data-connect's toolchain to Node 24, so this repack runs under its .nvmrc 24.21.0 rather than the Node 22.23.2 the #94 refresh used. (4) #113 `e10a79ba2` moved declared dependencies to their latest releases, which changes the packed inputs of BOTH packages again — a repin prepared against #112's merge would not have covered it, so the tarballs are repacked from #113's tree. (5) #116 `ed0dbaca5` regenerated both packages' artifact.json receipts, which #113 had left stale; that is the pinned commit. packages/polyfill-connectors/vendor/pdpp-collector-runtime-0.0.1.tgz moves to c8794cfa263d76d0487c2fa20aace62aef94b71f9bc667d9f476a5c8c8164ff1 and pdpp-connector-protocol-0.0.1.tgz off #94's 7a937c137 to d01bbbe0c177ba06bb4b0d9738d83dce193d566051c1493c40a8bf28cd95e4c2, with vendor/SHA256SUMS, vendor/README.md's duplicate digest block, and package-lock.json's two sha512 integrity entries all updated in the same commit — the lockfile records integrity for these path-referenced tarballs, so omitting it fails `npm ci` with EINTEGRITY. Both repacks were verified deterministic (two independent `npm pack` runs, byte-identical). Both new digests reproduce data-connect's OWN package receipts at this commit rather than merely agreeing with themselves: packages/connector-protocol/artifact.json records artifact_sha256 d01bbbe0c177ba06bb4b0d9738d83dce193d566051c1493c40a8bf28cd95e4c2 and packages/collector-runtime/artifact.json records c8794cfa263d76d0487c2fa20aace62aef94b71f9bc667d9f476a5c8c8164ff1, each byte-identical to the vendored tarball committed here. That two-sided confirmation is why the pin is ed0dbaca5 and not e10a79ba2: at e10a79ba2 BOTH receipts were stale (#113 moved the packed inputs without regenerating them, so artifact:verify failed for both packages, and collector-runtime's artifact:generate refused to run at all because it reads connector-protocol's committed receipt and saw the drift), leaving collector-runtime's digest backed only by repack determinism. data-connect#116 regenerated both receipts and changes NOTHING else — the diff e10a79ba2..ed0dbaca5 is exactly two files, packages/collector-runtime/artifact.json and packages/connector-protocol/artifact.json. Neither is packed: both packages declare files: ["dist/"], so artifact.json is outside the tarball and the vendored bytes are unchanged by the move. This repin is therefore a pin-and-provenance update, not a re-vendor; the two 0.0.1 tarballs committed here were packed at e10a79ba2 and a fresh repack at ed0dbaca5 reproduces their contents unchanged, confirmed by running drift job (c)'s own script. Drift jobs (a) collector-definitions, (d) reference-contract and (e) collector-packaging-manifest pass unmodified at this SHA, and (c) tarball-digests passes for this repo's vendor/SHA256SUMS, each verified by running the job's own script locally against a clean checkout of this commit. Known and NOT fixed here: pdpp's own vendor/SHA256SUMS still records pdpp-collector-runtime-0.0.1.tgz at the pre-#106 e274fb459, so job (c)'s pdpp leg fails until pdpp re-vendors that tarball — a change in pdpp, out of this PR's scope. data-connect#64 is NOT satisfied by this pin and needs its own later repin: it is still open, branched from the superseded 1577a34e5 pin, and has not been rebased onto #94 — its head would REVERSE #94's auth.ts and additionally moves packages/collector-runtime/artifact.json, so it must rebase and regenerate both receipts before it merges, and this repo repins again afterwards. Supersedes the temporary 27fe8086d pin, which tracked the unmerged branch chore/revendor-connectors-92 so the paired trees could be compared before #89 landed. A pin on an unmerged branch cannot stay valid: data-connect's consumer-drift-signal workflow requires the pinned commit to exist in its own checkout, and a pull-request merge ref cannot reach a commit that lives only on an unrelated branch. When #89 was rebased, 27fe8086d stopped being reachable from any ref, so every data-connect pull request touching a guarded path failed on the pin lookup regardless of what it changed. Pinning a merged main commit removes that failure mode. This SHA still carries data-connect#89's vendored malformed-line isolation and Claude/Codex symlink disclosure sources from data-connectors#92, unchanged by #94. Collector definitions are unchanged, and the separate 1.0.0 release pin remains unchanged. This pin also backs drift job (e) local-collector packaging manifest: it supplies packages/local-collector/tsconfig.build.json, the compile list that job compares against this repo's connector registry.

data-connect-1-0-0.note: A SEPARATE, later data-connect SHA used ONLY by the 1.0.0 half of drift job (c) tarball-digests — deliberately NOT the same value as the `data-connect` pin above. pdpp's vendor/SHA256SUMS (see pdpp's vendor/README.md 'Current 1.0.0 release-boundary pins') records pdpp-collector-runtime-1.0.0.tgz / pdpp-connector-protocol-1.0.0.tgz packed from data-connect PR #36's tree — this is PR #36's merge commit into main ('Add local collection and release checks', merged 2026-09-02T07:53:00Z), superseding the prior 10f25a3cd6 pin which recorded the PR's pre-merge head commit. Confirmed via `git diff 10f25a3cd6..b70dda89a -- packages/collector-runtime packages/connector-protocol scripts/pin-collector-runtime-protocol-dependency.ts` (empty — the merge is a true two-parent merge of the reviewed branch, not a squash, so the packages this pin backs are byte-identical between the two commits; the merge additionally picked up an unrelated repo-wide SPDX-header sweep and other main-tip drift, none of it touching these paths) that the previously-vendored 1.0.0 tarballs still reconcile: no re-vendor needed, this is a SHA-reference-only update. This SHA is NOT used for jobs (a)/(b) or the 0.0.1 tarball repack: data-connect's local-collector/collector-runtime/connector-protocol sources changed materially between the `data-connect` pin above and this one (STREAM_EVIDENCE outcomes-partition wire change, capability-array validation, package-artifact receipts), so reusing this SHA for the shared `data-connect` pin would flip jobs (a)/(b) and the 0.0.1 repack from passing to failing — those still compare against data-connectors' and pdpp's committed 0.0.1 artifacts, which were packed from the OLDER `data-connect` pin and have not been repinned to 1.0.0 themselves. Revisit consolidating these two pins into one only once data-connectors' own packages/polyfill-connectors/vendor/ moves off 0.0.1.

pdpp.note: Head of PDP-Connect/pdpp main on 2026-09-14, the merge of pdpp#361 'chore(vendor): drop the unused collector-runtime 0.0.1 archive', captured from main's head via `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` and confirmed an ancestor of main via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — never a PR head, for the reason the data-connect entry's superseded-pin history above records. Moved from 55c00d346 to unblock drift job (c) tarball-digests, whose pdpp leg has failed on every pull request in this repo since data-connect#106 landed. At 55c00d346, pdpp's vendor/SHA256SUMS recorded pdpp-collector-runtime-0.0.1.tgz at e274fb459cce011f3c290ab92a0d83252fa91af671d33e37e3809edea06fafbf, the digest of a tarball packed BEFORE #106 rewrote collector-runtime's durable outbox; job (c) repacks every recorded entry fresh from the `data-connect` pin above, so that entry could no longer reconcile and the leg reported 'FAIL: pdpp — pdpp-collector-runtime-0.0.1.tgz content manifest mismatch'. The fix belonged in pdpp, and pdpp#361 made it: the 0.0.1 archive was dead weight there — nothing in pdpp consumed it — so #361 deleted both the tarball and its SHA256SUMS line rather than re-vendoring bytes pdpp does not use. At this SHA pdpp's vendor/SHA256SUMS records only the two 1.0.0 release-boundary entries, which job (c) reproduces from the separate `data-connect-1-0-0` pin and which are unaffected by #106. Verified by running the job's own check-tarball-digest-drift.sh against clean clones at all four pinned SHAs: every leg passes, including this repo's own vendor/SHA256SUMS. Job (d) reference-contract compares identical bytes before and after this move — `git log 55c00d346..7fc529a64 -- packages/reference-contract` is empty, and the other eleven commits in that range touch only site content and docs — so the copied reference-contract modules are unchanged and the pin-freshness pdpp leg, which diffs that same path against pdpp's tracked ref, passes trivially with the pin now exactly at main's head. This is a pin-reference update only: no file in this repository changes besides this entry.
